PullRequest.Title: TypeScript: resolve Node from PATH when detecting the TS Server Node
PullRequest.Body:
When `js/ts.tsserver.node.path` (or `typescript.tsserver.nodePath`) is set to `node`, the TS extension detects a Node installation by spawning the bare command `node`. On Windows, a bare command name is also looked up in the current working directory before `PATH`, and the detection used the first workspace folder as its working directory.

This change resolves `node` to an absolute path using only the fully qualified `PATH` entries (drive-letter or UNC paths on Windows; relative entries such as `.` are skipped) and spawns that absolute path. The workspace folder is still used as the working directory for trusted workspaces, so version manager shims can pick the project's Node version. Explicitly configured absolute Node paths are unchanged.

**Changes**
- `extensions/typescript-language-features/src/utils/findExecutable.electron.ts`: new `findExecutableOnPath` helper.
- `extensions/typescript-language-features/src/configuration/configuration.electron.ts`: `findNodePath` uses it.
- `extensions/typescript-language-features/src/test/unit/findExecutable.test.ts`: unit tests.

**How to test**
1. Set the user setting `"js/ts.tsserver.node.path": "node"`.
2. Open a folder that contains a `.ts` file and open that file.
3. Check the TypeScript output channel: "Using Node installation from <absolute path on PATH> to run TS Server"; hover and completions work.

**Validation**
- `scripts\test-integration.bat --suite typescript`: passed (58 passing, 8 pending, 0 failing), including the new `findExecutableOnPath` tests.
- `gulp compile-extension:typescript-language-features`: passed (0 errors).
- `eslint` on the three changed files: passed.
- Manually verified in Code OSS on Windows that TS Server starts with the Node on `PATH` and IntelliSense works.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added synchronous I/O, loop cardinality, and activation/reconfiguration call paths are explicit in the code. Exact duration depends on PATH ordering and filesystem/network responsiveness, which affects severity rather than the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: synchronous filesystem metadata/access calls for every eligible PATH candidate
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each service-configuration load performs up to two synchronous probes per absolute Windows PATH entry before the first match (and one stat plus one access check per viable POSIX entry); the full scan repeats on initial JS/TS client creation and on every workspace configuration event, and can run twice when both workspace and global Node settings are `node`.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: blocked extension-host critical path and increased IntelliSense/configuration-change latency
Findings.PreviousBehavior: For a `node` setting, configuration loading directly called the existing `execFileSync('node', ...)`; it did not first issue a JavaScript-level synchronous filesystem probe for every PATH candidate.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new loop invokes `isExecutableFile` for every `.com`/`.exe` candidate until a match, and the default implementation uses synchronous `statSync`/`accessSync`. `loadFromWorkspace` reaches this on first supported-document activation and its unfiltered `onDidChangeConfiguration` listener reaches it again for every configuration change.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 39 places `isExecutableFile(candidate)` inside nested PATH-entry/extension loops; this entire filesystem search is new and executes before the pre-existing `execFileSync` Node detection.
Findings.Title: Cache the synchronous PATH resolution across configuration loads
Findings.Impact: Users who configure the TS server Node as `node` now block the extension host while PATH is scanned before TS Server setup. Long PATHs amplify the added I/O, and an absolute UNC/network entry before Node can make each synchronous probe slow, delaying initial IntelliSense and unrelated settings changes.
Findings.Evidence: `findExecutableOnPath` loops over every absolute PATH entry and calls `isExecutableFile(candidate)` here; the default at lines 60-64 performs synchronous filesystem calls. `ElectronServiceConfigurationProvider.findNodePath` calls this helper synchronously, `BaseServiceConfigurationProvider.loadFromWorkspace` reads both local/global Node paths, and `TypeScriptServiceClient` calls that loader in its constructor (line 186) and its broad configuration-change callback (lines 212-214). There is no result cache or coalescing.
Findings.Recommendation: Cache positive and negative resolutions keyed by the effective PATH value, platform, and executable name (or cache them in the provider while that key is unchanged), so configuration reloads and local/global reads reuse one scan while still rerunning the existing workspace-sensitive Node process check.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the first JavaScript/TypeScript document with `js/ts.tsserver.node.path` (or the deprecated setting) set to `node`.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Lazy client construction synchronously calls `loadFromWorkspace`, which must finish PATH resolution and the Node probe before the TS client can initialize and provide IntelliSense.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: `statSync` each candidate and, for a viable POSIX file, `accessSync` it for execute permission.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For A absolute entries before the first match, up to 2A candidate probes on Windows (`.com` and `.exe`); POSIX performs one stat per entry plus an access check for a file candidate. A miss scans all eligible entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No JavaScript-level filesystem scan preceded Node detection; configuration loading went directly to the subprocess probe.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All calls block lazy TS client startup and therefore delay initial language features.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one launch per configured scope; two when both effective workspace and global values independently equal `node`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One synchronous launch used bare `node`; the diff changes it to the resolved absolute path but does not introduce this subprocess boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before configuration is published; remains on the same critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number and ordering of absolute PATH entries after relative entries are filtered; local/global setting scopes can double the scan and launch.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fully serialized on the extension host: PATH candidates are checked one by one and then `execFileSync` runs; there is no limiter or off-critical-path scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No positive or negative cache exists. Even a warm extension process repeats the full filesystem resolution on the next configuration load.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the nested candidate loop, synchronous filesystem implementation, and lazy-client constructor path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Local PATH probes may be fast, but long PATHs and especially slow or disconnected absolute network entries can make synchronous probes visibly expensive; prevalence and exact duration vary by host.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the diff adds synchronous filesystem fan-out before an existing synchronous subprocess on the initial language-service critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change any workspace setting after the TS client is active while the configured Node value is `node`.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The unfiltered `onDidChangeConfiguration` callback synchronously reloads the entire service configuration before version managers and any server restart decision can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to the same full PATH scan for each configuration event, potentially once for each local/global `node` scope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every configuration event already relaunched the Node probe, but did not first perform this additional JS filesystem scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the extension host during unrelated setting changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One or two launches per event depending on configured scopes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same synchronous subprocess count existed, using the bare executable name.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the same callback after PATH scanning.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Absolute PATH entry count multiplied by configuration-event count and by one or two effective Node-setting scopes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each configuration event performs one serialized load; candidate filesystem calls and Node launches are synchronous, with no coalescing across events.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold and warm behavior are identical because successful paths and full misses are not retained; rapid events are not coalesced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the callback directly invokes `loadFromWorkspace` without checking affected settings, and the provider calls the new resolver for each effective `node` value.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Configuration events are user/workflow dependent, while PATH and network latency determine each added scan's duration.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable as repeated boundary fan-out; caching by effective PATH would preserve semantics while removing repeated scans.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use the bundled Node or configure an explicit absolute Node path.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration still validates an explicit path synchronously, but the new PATH resolver branch is not entered; bundled Node uses no configured-path detection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing `existsSync`/`lstatSync` validation of an explicit configured path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existence check and at most one metadata check per explicit local/global path load.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same explicit-path validation existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous configuration validation, unchanged by this diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most the number of explicit local/global configured paths; no PATH-entry scaling from the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No diff-introduced work or concurrency for these branches.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing validation is uncached, but the new helper is not called.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: `findNodePath` is called only when the selected setting value exactly equals `node`.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material to the changed behavior.
Scenarios.Verdict: No diff-caused performance regression on the default or explicit-absolute-path branches.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all three changed files and traced initial lazy activation, configuration reloads, successful/missing PATH lookup, and unchanged explicit/default paths. Submitted one medium-severity finding for uncached synchronous filesystem fan-out added ahead of the existing Node subprocess probe.
